 Shri Prateek Kulshrestha - Advocate for appellant.
 Shri S.S. Kushwaha - Government Advocate for the State.

Order 
1.

This miscellaneous second appeal under Section 71(6) of Food Safety and Standards Act has been filed against the order dated 19/9/2024 passed by Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/First District Judge Morena in MCA No.25/2024 as well as order dated 4/3/2024 passed by Adjudicating Authority/Additional District Magistrate Morena in case No.19/2022/Food Safety.
2.

entities.text: Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/First District Judge Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The facts necessary for disposal of present appeal in short are that on 13.02.2021 at about 3:15 pm, the Food Safety Officer carried out the inspection of Neha Kirana store and found that 15 kg of moong dal and 14 kg of besan were kept in a loose condition.
Since the Food Safety Officer had suspicion about the quality of moong dal and besan, therefore, he collected the samples and sent it to the Food Analyst.
The Food Analyst by his report informed that the moong dal was found to be of substandard quality.
Accordingly, the report of the Food Analyst was sent to the appellant.
He did not prefer an appeal under Section 46(4) of the Food Safety and Standards Act and accordingly the complaint was filed.

The Adjudicating Authority by order dated 04/03/2024 held the appellant guilty of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:33719 2 MSA-16-2024 violating Section 51 of Food Safety and Standards Act and imposed a fine of Rs.2 lakhs.
3.

Being aggrieved by the order passed by the Adjudicating Authority, the appellant preferred an appeal which has been partially allowed by the appellate authority and the penalty of 2 lakh was Rakesh Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69141620/
1 reduced to Rs.1 lakh.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Challenging the order passed by the authorities below, it is submitted by counsel for the appellant that appellant was not given sufficient time to lead defence evidence.

The appellant is a petty trader,
and therefore, the penalty of Rs.1 lakh is on higher side.
5. Per contra, counsel for the State has supported the findings recorded by the Authorities below.

6. Considered the submissions made by counsel for the parties.
7.
From the order sheet dated 17/1/2024 recorded by the Adjudicating Authority, it is clear that the prosecution closed its evidence on 17/1/2024.
Thereafter the case was fixed for recording of defense witness on 6/2/2024 and 22/2/2024.
On 22/02/2024, counsel for the appellant expressed his inability to lead any defence evidence, and accordingly, the case was closed.
Counsel for the appellant could not point out any provision of law which requires the authority to grant multiple opportunities to a wrongdoer to lead evidence.
Once on 22/2/2024, the appellant had expressed his inability to lead defence evidence, then it was not expected from the Adjudicating Authority to adjourn the matter.
Even the appellant did not offer himself to be a defence witness in his defence.
8. Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that the Adjudicating Authority did not commit any mistake by closing the right of the appellant to lead evidence.
The appellant did not file any appeal against the report NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:33719 3 MSA-16-2024 of the Food Analyst.
Moong daal is a pulse ( daal) which is generally used by all sections of the society as the said pulse is easily digestible.

Selling a substandard food article meant for human consumption cannot be looked into in a lenient manner, specifically when it was never claimed by the appellant that he is selling substandard food articles thereby giving an opportunity to the consumers to either purchase or not to purchase.
9. Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that the Authorities below did not commit any mistake by awarding a penalty of Rs.1 lakh.
The appellate authority has already shown much leniency and no further leniency can be shown by this Court.

10. With the aforesaid observations, the order dated 19/9/2024 passed by Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/First District Judge Morena in MCA No.25/2024 as well as order dated 4/3/2024 passed by Adjudicating Authority/Additional District Magistrate Morena in case No.19/2022/Food Safety are hereby affirmed.
